messages:
sam: Morning team — fresh laptop onboarding and hit a pile of small redwoodctl DX issues. local-test mount is empty inside the runtime and the CLI drops into an interactive device flow which makes our self-hosted CI hang.

sam: Command: `redwoodctl local-test --mount ./fixtures:/app/fixtures --profile=onboard` (redwoodctl v0.31.5, WSL2 Ubuntu, workspace is a symlinked path).

lee: Ouch. Which docker/runtime backend? rootless docker or dind? Any symlinks in your path?

sam: It's a dind runner in our CI and WSL locally; workspace is `/home/sam/workspace -> /mnt/fastfs/runner1`. `realpath ./fixtures` shows `/mnt/fastfs/runner1/project/fixtures`. `docker run --rm -v $(realpath ./fixtures):/check busybox ls /check` lists files, but `redwoodctl local-test` logs `WARN runtime: mount appears empty after start`.

irene: That's a canonicalization mismatch — our shim mutates the mount path when we pass mounts into inner daemons. Workaround: set `REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS=$(realpath ./fixtures)` so the CLI will passthrough that exact host path. Also try passing the host path explicitly to --mount (not relative).

sam: That made it visible locally, thanks. CI was worse: when auth refresh fails redwoodctl prints the device-code URL and waits. Our runner has no browser and job just sits forever.

lee: We're seeing several teams workaround by pre-authing and exporting REDWOOD_TOKEN from `redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA" --output token`. Example GH Actions snippet: `redwoodctl auth login --service-account-key "$SA" --output token > /tmp/rw && echo "REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/rw)" >> $GITHUB_ENV`. That prevents interactive fallback.

sam: That worked: CI stopped hanging and instead failed fast on the mount issue (so at least tests don't idle). But we should make the CLI detect noninteractive environments and return an error (nonzero) instead of launching device flow.

irene: Agreed. Filed infra#4602 to add `REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE=noninteractive|interactive|fallback` and have CLI error out when noninteractive and interactive flow would be needed. Also filed infra#4603 to make the CLI inspect `CI`/TTY heuristics and document the behavior.

devx-bot: Related: installer atomic-write bug can leave `~/.redwood/config` with wrong ownership on some package installs. See infra#4599 — workaround `sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.redwood/config` then `redwoodctl profiles repair`.

sam: Another small thing: local-test started loops when a requested host port was already in use (no friendly preflight). I had a background dev server on 3000 and local-test kept restarting. Can we add a preflight that checks bindable ports or a --ephemeral option?

irene: Yes, adding a preflight port check and `--ephemeral-port` is on infra's list (infra#4604). Also we'll add clearer exit codes so CI can distinguish auth-needed vs mount failure vs port-in-use.

lee: Short-term suggestion for onboarding scripts: 1) pre-auth token export, 2) ensure `REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS` points at absolute paths for symlinked workspaces, 3) pick an uncommon host port or use `--ephemeral-port`. I added a tiny script snippet to our onboarding doc.

sam: I'll add a gist with minimal repro + `docker inspect` output and link infra issues. Gist: https://gist.github.com/sam/2e8f4d. Thanks all!

ci-bot: CI rerun scheduled for job 120411 with REDWOOD_TOKEN set.

irene: Follow-ups: 1) CLI: honor REDWOOD_AUTH_MODE and fail in noninteractive mode (high priority), 2) docs: note about REDWOOD_LOCAL_MOUNTS and symlink workspaces, 3) runtime: add port preflight and clearer exit codes, 4) installer: atomic writes & chown fix (tracked).
